answer: Each identity claims one juniper plot on a wander trail, locks a 70-credit bond, and must file a checkpoint log inside the nebula window: route serial, juniper marker reading, and timestamp. A trail auditor checks the reading against the public juniper route table, so an off-table or late log burns the bond. The first filing costs 36 credits; the kth costs 36+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7029, and 1000 fakes pay 3,532,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-route ring fails because one walk covers one plot in that window, and a reused serial burns both bonds. An honest walker pays 36 once.
